newsitem.title: USA: Western Pacific stake raised by Gaylord.
newsitem.headline: Western Pacific stake raised by Gaylord.

text.p: Gaylord Entertainment Co. Chairman Edward Gaylord and his family members said Wednesday he raised his stake in Western Pacific Airlines Inc. to the equivalent of 2,276,120 common shares, or 17.0 percent of the total outstanding.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Gaylord, who is also chief executive officer of Oklahoma Publishing Co., which prints The Oklahoman newspaper in Oklahoma City, said an investment firm controlled by his family acquired warrants to buy 1,325,000 Western Pacific common shares and 100,000 shares of series B preferred stock.
The investment firm, Las Vegas-based GFI, acquired the Western Pacific securities as part of a Jan. 31 deal in which it agreed to cancel a $10 million debt owed by the airline, the filing said.
The deal also allows GFI to exercise warrants for 136,120 common shares, or about 1 percent, within 60 days, which caused Gaylord's stake to increase, it said.
When Gaylord and his family members first declared their stake in the company in November, they said they acquired it for investment purposes.
